text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- After reconsidering their decision, the members of the opposition have confirmed their one-month boycott of Parliament.
- Will the Zagreb county assembly be discussing the sacking of its president Zdravko Tomac at its session on Wednesday?
- A recent survey carried out among Croats shows their concern about salaries and total disinterest in the state of the firms they work for.

- The proposed changes to the penal code: If accepted the longest jail sentences will be increased from 20 to 30 years and the article on the banning of public appearances used during the communist era to clamp down on public appearances of opposition politicians will be scrapped.
- The session of the parliament's investigation commission: 44,000 tons of wheat have vanished.

- Dalmatinska banka Zadar explains that the fact that it had closed a 20 million German marks deal on an EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction Development) loan proves that the investigation being launched against its senior staff is unfounded. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
